findings.claim: The diff changes the start-placement trigger in useSceneList, which is outside the touch points. The placement now runs once per resetKey (placedKeyRef), no longer on every shown/fileId/rows change, and it is now gated on a new `layoutSettled` input fed from the Container's awaitingVisual. Because placedKeyRef is never cleared on hide, a .loft that is hidden and shown again with the same frames gets no start placement and no new opening.
findings.impact: Hiding and re-showing the Scenes panel of a YouTube .loft (the host turns `active` off and on, so the frames are kept) leaves opening ended once the reader has scrolled. The re-shown list's near tiles then wait D (200 ms) instead of loading at once. A failed tile is not asked for at once after that start event. The playing row is not placed again on re-show: the list comes back at its top, and if following was off it does not move to the playing row.
findings.evidence: useSceneList.ts:163-165: resetKey = `${fileId}|${shown?1:0}|${starts}`. useSceneList.ts:348 returns early while !shown, so placedKeyRef keeps the shown key 'f|1|…'. useSceneList.ts:351-354: on re-show the key equals placedKeyRef, so it only calls syncVisible; openingRef/setOpening(true) (355-357) and setFollowing(true)/placeRow (358-368) are skipped. For a .loft, the Container keeps rows on hide (ScenesSectionContainer.tsx:296 returns before any reset; rows are set to null only on collapse and file change for native). So resetKey is identical on re-show. Native panels are not affected, because loadNative (ScenesSectionContainer.tsx:249) sets rows to null and the intermediate key 'f|1|' differs. useScenePictures.ts:98-112 then resets `requested` and calls read() with opening=false, so every near tile starts a dwell. Before this change the placement effect depended on [shown, fileId, rows] and placed again on every show.
findings.repro: Not run (read-only reviewer). Mental trace of the I8 `.loft` row of ScenesSectionPictureTiming.test.tsx: open, wheelTo(6*ROW) ends opening, rerender active:false then active:true, now() twice with no time advanced. read() runs with opening=false, so t=5 only starts a dwell, and `expect(srcs()).toContain('/scene-tile/f1?t=5')` should fail. If that test passes, something I did not see resets placedKeyRef. Mutation check: clearing placedKeyRef.current when !shown at useSceneList.ts:348 would restore the per-show placement and opening.

bucket_proposal.reason: I8 requires a failed .loft tile to be asked for again after the next start event. Becoming active is a start event (Terms), so §1.5 and I1 opening behaviour should apply; on a .loft re-show this code gives a dwell instead, and does no start placement.

findings.proposed_fix: Reset placedKeyRef and pendingSettleRef when shown turns false, e.g. in the placement effect's `!shown` branch, so that every showing is a new start event; or keep `shown` transitions out of the dedup key.

findings.claim: The diff adds a new input to useSceneList, `layoutSettled` (from the Container's `awaitingVisual`), which holds the start reading until the Visual Index answer arrives. The touch points describe useSceneList's readings only as 'after the start placement, scroll, resize, c or row-step change' and do not mention a wait on the Visual Index.
findings.impact: With the policy on and a slow Visual Index answer, `ready` stays false during opening for a native panel. No picture is asked for until that answer lands, which delays the 'at once' opening pictures by the server's Visual Index latency.
findings.evidence: ScenesSectionContainer.tsx:450-458 passes layoutSettled: !awaitingVisual. useSceneList.ts:374-375 defers placedKey while !layoutSettled. useSceneList.ts:399 keeps deferring while !layoutSettled && opening. useScenePictures.ts:63 returns while !ready.

bucket_proposal.reason: Unplanned coupling; under the spec's definition, a reading before the start placement's own measurement is not a reading, so this arguably fits I1.

Listed but not touched: ScenesSectionOneList.test.tsx, ScenesSectionLoftVisualIndex.test.tsx and projects.ts. projects.ts does not need a change, because non-desktop specs run in the phone project by default.
The new e2e file scenes-picture-timing.spec.ts is registered in spec-viewport.spec.ts AT_THE_PHONE_WIDTH, as the touch points require.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Start placement is now deduplicated by resetKey, including the frame start times. Frames refetched with the same starts no longer place the list again; the spec's Terms treat this as not an arrival, but it also changes SPEC-ADDON-152 §1.3 placement behaviour.
The opening's at-once request waits for the Visual Index answer on native panels with the policy on (F4).
regression_risks: A .loft panel hidden and re-shown by the host: no start placement and no new opening (F1).
Start placement now depends on layoutSettled: when the Visual Index answer arrives during opening and the pending reading has not completed, the placement effect re-runs and places the list again.
test_coverage: The I6 re-show test covers only a native panel, where loadNative nulls the rows and so changes resetKey. No test re-shows a .loft after opening has ended and asserts the at-once request or the placement, apart from the I8 .loft row, which by my reading should fail.
No test covers a slow Visual Index answer delaying the opening pictures.
